title: WPSS/936/2014 of Harish Singh Bisht Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.936 (S/S) of 2014
Harish Singh Bisht Ö Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö.Ö Respondents
Present: Mr. T.P.S. Takuli, Advocate present for the petitioner.
 Mr. N.P. Shah, learned Standing Counsel, present for the
State/respondent no.1.
 Mr. B.D. Upadhyay, Senior Advocate, assisted by Ms. Manta
Bisht, Advocate, present for respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner before this Court is an employee of
Kumaon University. He was appointed on contract basis on
consolidated salary as a Class III employee on 01.11.2003.
Admittedly, he has been working against a substantive
vacancy of Class III post since his initial date of appointment.
Now the Government of Uttarakhand has framed
Regularization Rules which are meant for the regularization
of such employees, which are known as ìRegularization of
Employees appointed on Daily Wage, Work Charge, Contract,
Fixed Pay, Part Time and on Adhoc Basis, Rules 2013î.
These rules have been adopted by the University, which is
represented before this Court by Senior Advocate Mr. B.D.
Upadhyay. The petitioner, however, has been declined
regularization even though he has completed 10 years of
service and juniors to him (who were on daily rated basis)
have been regularized. Hence, aggrieved the petitioner has
filed the present writ petition.
2. In the counter affidavit it has been brought before
this Court that at the time when petitioner was engaged on
daily rated basis, his age was 35 years 04 months and 27
days, as has been precisely stated by the petitioner and

2
admitted by the learned Senior Advocate Mr. B.D. Upadhyay.
The maximum age limit for appointment on a class III post in
the University at the relevant time was 35 years. Therefore,
under Rule 4 (2) of the Regularization Rules, 2013 such an
employee who does not fulfill the conditions of appointment
including the age is not liable to be regularized.
3. On the other hand, the petitioner contends that it
is nobodyís case that petitioner had misrepresented his age.
He has clearly stated the exact age at the time of initial
appointment and he is working on a substantive post for the
last more than 10 years. As per the provisions of the
Regularization Rules, he is liable to be regularized. Moreover
even if the question of age has now come up, the same is
liable to be considered under Rule 7 of the Regularization
Rules 2013. Under the Rule 7, the powers have been given to
the University to relax the upper age limit in a given case.
The learned Senior Counsel who is representing the
University further states that such a provision contained in
Rule 7 will only be applicable when the candidate is
exceeding the upper age limit at the time of regularization.
However, if a candidate exceeded the age limit even at the
time of initial appointment, Rule 7 will not come to his
rescue.
4. Rule 7 provides for grant of relaxation of the upper
age limit at the time of regularization. Whether the upper age
limit can be relaxed at the time of initial entry or at the time
when regularization is taking place is not clear. It can be
interpreted both ways. However, this Court is of the opinion
that the meaning which is beneficial for the petitioner such a
meaning is liable to be given to Rule 7 and since there is
authority to relax the rules and the petitioner is working for
the last more than 10 years and he has exceeded the upper
age limit for 04 months 27 days which is admitted by the

3
respondent/University, this Court is of the considered view
that non consideration of the case of the petitioner is totally
arbitrary and infact is not justified.
6. In view of the above facts and circumstances, the
writ petition is allowed. A mandamus is issued to the
respondent/University to regularize the services of the
petitioner, subject to the fact that the petitioner is otherwise
eligible.
7. No order as to costs.
